name: supplier-compare-agent
subtitle: Supplier comparison and purchasing decision support
role: Team project · Show Me Your Token
summary: A decision-support agent that turns supplier quotes into comparable evidence. Code produces a reference ranking, the agent makes a recommendation using read-only tools, and a buyer approves or overrides it.
highlights: A four-person team project for the NUS-ISS “Show Me Your Agent” hackathon, demonstrated with synthetic supplier data.
Normalizes price, lead time, payment terms, on-time delivery and quality; applies hard constraints before calculating reference scores and negotiation gaps.
Calls a model through an Ollama-compatible gateway and parses JSON tool requests. The agent may depart from the reference ranking when supported by tool evidence; structured output is validated.
Treats quote text as untrusted input, with injection detection, read-only tools, supplier eligibility checks, fallback behavior, and normal and adversarial evaluation cases.
Logs model recommendations, buyer approvals or override reasons, and request IDs. The system recommends; it never places orders.

name: no-buzzwords
subtitle: Writing rules and evaluation tools for coding assistants
summary: An installable skill and plugin that asks coding assistants to explain mechanisms and use concrete examples. Evaluation checks that clearer wording preserves technical accuracy.
highlights: Ten writing rules target vague wording and unnecessary jargon while preserving precise terminology and an appropriate register for expert readers.
Provides a skill, Claude Code plugin configuration and an optional always-on hook for different assistant workflows.
Python scripts manage test cases and a scoring rubric, with reproducible shuffling and anonymization of responses for blind evaluation.
Uses correctness as a separate release gate: a drop greater than 0.1 from the baseline fails the gate even if the total score improves. Cases also test oversimplification and expert contexts.
Provides continuous-integration checks and offline validation of test cases and scoring rules without model calls or credentials.

name: HRTI
subtitle: Human Replaceability Type Indicator
summary: A self-assessment experiment about work tasks. It examines routine, knowledge, responsibility and physical presence to help people reflect on the division of work between humans and AI.
highlights: Uses 28 questions across four axes: task routine, knowledge codifiability, responsibility for consequences, and embodied presence. Their combinations produce 16 types.
Includes reverse-scored questions, with feedback loops and bargaining position recorded as additional labels rather than determinants of the type.
Built with native HTML, JavaScript and Canvas. The questionnaire, scoring and result-image generation run in the browser without a backend.
Anonymous telemetry is disabled by default. Results are not validated probabilities of replacement or career predictions.

name: coding-agent-from-scratch
subtitle: A terminal coding agent, built from first principles
summary: A command-line coding assistant built without an agent framework. Repository maps, sandbox escape tests and A/A controls put each design decision to the test.
highlights: A native tool-calling ReAct loop with seven tools. SEARCH/REPLACE editing uses a four-tier matching chain to handle whitespace and partial-line drift. Shell commands run inside macOS Seatbelt, with boundaries verified by escape tests: about 1,300 lines of core code and 52 tests, including nine escape tests.

The repository map uses tree-sitter definitions and references to build a file graph, then personalized PageRank to rank context for the task. Constraining edges by actual Python imports raised edge precision from 32% to 100% without dropping a true edge. IDF-weighted seeds addressed query understanding.
On a 112-file repository, the map reduced task steps by 21% and input tokens by 33%. These figures describe that controlled experiment, not a guarantee across repositories.

The evaluation harness runs an A/A arm by default, putting effects beside their noise floor; this led me to retract an earlier claim. In this architecture, output caps made history compression unnecessary. Sub-agent isolation used 42% more total tokens for 22% less main-loop context, without improving completion or correctness. Committed traces make the measurements reproducible.

name: bodycraft-oss
subtitle: Multi-path retrieval with measured scoring weights
summary: Five retrieval paths, visible score breakdowns and repeatable experiments replace opaque weighting with a measurable ranking problem.
highlights: Runs filename and path, section title, SQLite FTS5, dense-vector and entity-graph retrieval in parallel. Four independent weighting strategies score the results, which merge per file with per-path scores exposed.

Moves hard-coded scoring parameters into hot-reloadable configuration. Files the model actually opens provide weak relevance labels, with provenance recorded so they are not mistaken for human annotations.

Optimizes NDCG rather than ratio-style metrics that can improve by collapsing weight onto a single path while the ranking worsens. Grid search maps the space; repeated independent genetic-algorithm runs separate gains from noise.
Index schemas, configuration and ranking metrics are covered by 17 tests. The pipeline runs offline without an API key.

name: Internal spreadsheet Q&A platform
subtitle: Conversational spreadsheet analysis
summary: Turns natural-language questions over uploaded spreadsheets into verified SQL, result tables and charts. Structured plans, whitelisted actions and role-based isolation define what the system can execute.
highlights: A FastAPI and SQLAlchemy backend spans 76 modules, 23,331 lines and 56 test files, using MySQL, Redis, MinIO and Qwen. A 7,487-line React 19 front end streams over SSE. Rolled out to 20+ internal pilot users, whose trial feedback estimated roughly two hours of manual work saved per person per day.

Refactored a fixed LLM workflow into a Planner–Executor design. The planner emits only a structured plan: intent, target fields, actions, constraints and failure policy. The executor runs whitelisted actions over read-only SQL with table, field and permission checks.
Persists session context, generated SQL and chart configuration so follow-up questions can refer to earlier turns. Data isolation follows organization and role boundaries.

Co-authored the invention disclosure, filed in June 2026 and under examination. The pre-execution gate is S = 0.35F + 0.25A + 0.20C + 0.10P + 0.10R, with access compliance A a hard gate. Later rebuilt the core as a native tool in an open-source agent runtime, exposing only a controlled clarify / result_table / result_chart protocol.

name: Hybrid UAV Energy Management
summary: Designed and implemented the core energy-management algorithms for a hybrid-powered UAV.
highlights: Combined rule-based control with model predictive control to allocate power across multiple energy sources during flight.
Built system-level simulation and analysis workflows to examine power output, energy use and control response, then used the results to tune the allocation strategy.
Iterated algorithms and validated control policies to improve power-use efficiency and operating stability in representative mission conditions.
The project was selected for a national undergraduate innovation programme and received dedicated funding, spanning requirements, algorithm design, simulation and milestone evaluation.

name: Breadify
subtitle: A mobile app for bread enthusiasts
summary: Led the product design of Breadify, a mobile app for people who enjoy discovering and sharing bread.
highlights: Worked through the full UX process: user research, problem definition, ideation, prototyping and testing, with a focus on discovery, interaction and personal records.
Designed high-fidelity interactive prototypes and organized more than ten user tests. Qualitative feedback and usability observations guided five major design iterations.
Received the course’s People’s Choice award.

name: KAIST Smart Canteen
summary: Led the prototype design of a context-aware campus dining system at KAIST.
highlights: Defined requirements, system design and implementation around five campus dining scenarios, modelling user context and environmental changes.
Designed and built the Web interface and integrated the IoT platform to ingest, synchronize and visualize live data.
Created a high-fidelity mobile prototype in Figma, showing dining-space layout, crowd density and food options to support dining decisions and operational analysis.
